column2: WorkforceOS Section 3 - Data Analysts: Workforce Analytics & BI Dashboard   |   Zenith Nova Technologies (fictional)   |   Cut-off 30 Sep 2026

Everything in this file is FICTIONAL. The company "Zenith Nova Technologies Pvt Ltd", its people, clients, vendors, e-mails and numbers were generated for training. Any resemblance to real persons or businesses is accidental. Tax, PF, ESI and professional-tax rules are SAMPLE values for learning; never use them for real payroll.

This workbook is one of three that were built from ONE shared simulated company (the "master dataset"). The same employee ids, departments, payroll runs and ledger numbers appear in all three workbooks, so work done by the Python, AI/ML and Data teams lines up row for row.

A ready-made star-schema warehouse extract for the Data team: calendar, employee (with history), department, role and other dimensions; payroll, attendance, leave, headcount, ledger, invoice, expense and task facts; AI feeds (anomalies, attrition risk, forecasts); governance sheets (metric dictionary, data contracts, quality checks); budgets and targets; and an answer key. The facts contain a small number of deliberately planted problems so that your data-quality checks have something to find.

column2: •  Use employee_key (not employee_id) to join facts to dim_employee so that history is respected: a person who moved department in June must appear in the old department before June.

•  The sheets reconciliation_answer_key and reference_summary_dept_month contain the CORRECT monthly totals computed from clean data. Use them to test your pipeline. Your own totals from the fact sheets will differ in the months touched by planted problems until you clean them.
•  The sheet dq_known_issues lists every planted problem with record ids. Write your checks first (see dq_checks_catalog for ideas), then compare.

•  fact_task, fact_anomaly, fact_attrition_risk and fact_forecast are SAMPLE feeds that stand in for the Full Stack task board and the AI services until they are live. Their contracts are in data_contracts. In Task 19 you replace them with live APIs.
•  Show aggregates only. The metric dictionary gives a minimum group size; hide smaller groups (a group of one reveals one person pay).
•  Salary data is sensitive; it appears only in fact_payroll, so you can practise column- and row-level access control.
•  Dates: date_key is an integer YYYYMMDD. dim_date covers 2020-2026 with Indian financial year and fiscal quarter (Q1 = April to June).
